unit_text: On Tuesday I reread Jonah's note about the audit appeal and copied two figures from the draft budget into the email to Mara before the meeting with Selene, our legal lead.
I kept wondering whether he had sent the note to protect me, to warn Mara, or to pin the delay on me
my chest tightened when the note itself only said, "we need to talk before lunch."
During the meeting with Selene, our legal lead
I admitted I still hadn't sent the correction memo to the vendor
apologized for freezing during Friday's client walkthrough.
Afterward I opened the unsent reply to Jonah
deleted one sentence
restored it
kept hearing Noor laugh from the scene in the essay where the child drops the bowl.
I couldn't tell whether I was angry at Noor, at the essay, or at the part of me that keeps treating every paragraph like a verdict.
The rest of the evening was me arguing with my own roadmap.
I wrote "stability is a promise we make to strangers" in the margin
crossed it out
rewrote the last line
compared the failure table to last night's trace.
I still didn't know whether the bug belonged in the cache, in the queue, or in my assumptions.
At dinner with my brother he asked whether the scan had frightened me again.
I told him I was okay
I wasn't
I could barely swallow.
Before sleep I listened to the voicemail from Dr. Imani
did not call back
kept telling myself I already knew what it said.
I don't.
If I call back, it will be about the scan
if I don't, it will still be about the scan.
